🤖 AI Fix Suggestion
🔍 Root Cause
The "Previous slide" button has a disabled="" attribute hardcoded or incorrectly applied in the website source code. This attribute makes the button non-interactable regardless of its visual appearance. The button appears partially visible (opacity: 0.5) suggesting it was intended to look inactive only on the first slide, but the disabled state is being incorrectly persisted or initialized — it should only be disabled when the slideshow is genuinely at the first slide, and must be re-enabled as soon as the user can navigate backwards. The disabled attribute is preventing any click interaction entirely.

  • **Verify initialization order**: ensure the slideshow JS initializes the current slide index correctly before applying any disabled states — a likely bug is that the controller sets disabled on load and fails to remove it when navigating forward
  • **Fix the opacity style**: use CSS to style the disabled state (e.g., .slideshow-control[disabled] { opacity: 0.5; }) rather than leaving opacity at 0.5 permanently, so the visual state correctly reflects the interactive state
